name: Packet
tagline: See what your network is doing.

description.project: A desktop network monitor that displays active connections, summarizes interface traffic, and helps users inspect network activity from one place.
description.technical: Cross-platform desktop application built with Tauri, Rust, and React. Rust commands collect operating-system network information and expose normalized data to a TypeScript frontend, which presents connection details and traffic history.

features.name: Active connection inspector
features.description: Displays active network connections with protocol, local address, remote address, and connection state.
features.implementation: Collected connection information in the Rust backend, normalized platform-specific records into a shared application model, and exposed the result through Tauri commands for the frontend to query.

features.name: Traffic history
features.description: Visualizes upload and download activity over time for available network interfaces.
features.implementation: Sampled interface byte counters at fixed intervals, calculated throughput from differences between consecutive samples, and passed timestamped measurements to the charting layer.

features.name: Connection filtering
features.description: Allows users to narrow the connection list by protocol, process name, and remote address.
features.implementation: Added composable frontend filters over the normalized connection model and kept filter state in the interface so users can combine criteria without requesting a new system scan for each change.

highlights: Bridged operating-system network data from a Rust backend to a React interface.
Calculated network throughput from periodic interface counter samples.
Built searchable and filterable views for active network connections.
